title: Control of pickerel weed in rice crop fields - Vietnam

Header: Control of pickerel weed in rice crop fields - Vietnam
Monochoria vaginalis Rau mác lá thon, rau mác bao

Prevention: Control established weed populations near waterways to prevent spread during flooding and storm events.
Clean equipment and farm machinery after working in infested areas to prevent seeds and stolons being spread.
Use water from a source that's free of the weed for watering and flooding.
Use rotation between rice and upland crops every growing season, if applicable.
It is often practicable to cultivate upland crops during the winter season.
Monitoring: A fleshy, tufted, annual or perennial aquatic herb (10-50cm high) with a glabrous, shiny appearance and a short rhizome.
It forms rosettes and spreads by short stolons.
Flowers in spikes (3-6cm long), each with 6 violet or lilac tepals (the outer parts of the flower) which spread at flowering and later are spirally contorted.
Inspect fields weekly or fortnightly and implement direct control when seedlings or larger plants are found.
Check for the weed in wetlands and along waterways in the area.
Water and storm events can spread seeds.
Direct Control: The weed is not difficult to remove by hand, but requires persistence to remove successive flushes of germination.

In submerged conditions, the majority of seedlings emerge within a short space of time, with a germination peak 15-25 days after seeds are shed - promote weed germination (drain off the water after ploughing), then remove weeds by hand or control by use of a post- emergence herbicide (glyphosate) when weeds are 2-3 weeks old.
